title: "data_process_incident_weather"

## 1. Data

The study area covers PeMS districts D7, D8, and D12 in April 2026. Four datasets are used: Station Metadata, Station 5-Minute, CHP Incident, and NOAA GHCNh Weather. Variables used in the HTML are marked in blue.

### 1.1 *Station Metadata*

Station Metadata describes the location and road attributes of each PeMS detector station.

* <span style="color: blue;">**ID**</span>: PeMS station ID. It links metadata to the Station 5-Minute records.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Fwy**</span>: Freeway or route number.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Dir**</span>: Travel direction, such as northbound, southbound, eastbound, or westbound.

* **District**: Caltrans district number.

* **County** and **City**: FIPS location codes.

* **State_PM**: State postmile label.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Abs_PM**</span>: Absolute postmile. Stations on the same freeway and direction are ordered with this value.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Latitude**</span> and <span style="color: blue;">**Longitude**</span>: Station coordinates.

* **Length**: Road length represented by the station, in miles.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Type**</span>: Station type. `ML` means mainline. Only mainline stations are used for the coloured road links.

* **Lanes**: Number of lanes observed by the station.

* **Name**: Station name or nearby road name.

* **User_ID_1** to **User_ID_4**: Other station identifiers supplied by PeMS.

### 1.2 *Station 5-Minute*

Station 5-Minute contains one row for each station and 5-minute interval.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Timestamp**</span>: Beginning of the 5-minute interval.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Station**</span>: PeMS station ID.

* <span style="color: blue;">**District**</span>: Caltrans district number.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Freeway**</span>: Freeway or route number.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Direction**</span>: Travel direction.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Lane Type**</span>: Station category. Only `ML` records are used in the HTML.

* **Station Length**: Road length represented by the station.

* **Samples**: Number of detector samples received during the interval. It is checked as a data-quality indicator but does not remove a valid average-speed value.

* **Percentage Observed**: Share of expected observations that were received. It is checked as a data-quality indicator but does not remove a valid average-speed value.

* **Total Flow**: Total vehicles counted during the interval.

* **Average Occupancy**: Percentage of time that the detector was occupied.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Average Speed**</span>: Average station speed during the interval, in mph.

The remaining columns repeat samples, flow, occupancy, speed, and observation status for each lane. The HTML uses the station-level average speed rather than the individual lane values.

Stations are grouped by district, freeway, and direction, then ordered by absolute postmile. Two neighbouring mainline stations form one road link. The speed assigned to a link is the mean of the available speeds at its two endpoints.

### 1.3 *CHP Incident*

The CHP data have two record types. The incident summary gives one row per event. The detail data contain timestamped CHP log messages for the same incident IDs. Both record types are used.

The incident summary contains:

* <span style="color: blue;">**Incident ID**</span>: CHP incident identifier.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Timestamp**</span>: Time when the incident was reported.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Description**</span>: CHP event description.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Location**</span> and <span style="color: blue;">**Area**</span>: Text description of the incident location.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Latitude**</span> and <span style="color: blue;">**Longitude**</span>: Incident coordinates.

* <span style="color: blue;">**District**</span>, <span style="color: blue;">**Freeway**</span>, and <span style="color: blue;">**Direction**</span>: Route information.

* **County FIPS** and **City FIPS**: Administrative location codes.

* **State Postmile**: Caltrans postmile label.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Absolute Postmile**</span>: Numeric postmile used to match the event to a road link.

* **Severity**: Severity value when supplied by CHP.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Duration**</span>: Reported event duration, in minutes.

Descriptions are grouped into collision, disabled vehicle, traffic hazard, construction or closure, fire, and other events. An event is treated as active from its report time to the end of its duration. A missing or non-positive duration is replaced with 30 minutes.

Incidents are matched to road links by district, freeway, direction, and absolute postmile. A postmile match is kept when the gap is no more than 1 mile. Coordinates are used when postmile matching is unavailable, with a maximum gap of 3 kilometres. CHP does not identify the exact affected lane.

The detail messages are joined by incident ID. Dispatch status messages such as `Unit Assigned`, `Unit Enroute`, and `Unit At Scene` are removed. Repeated messages are removed, and up to three messages describing vehicles, blocked lanes, or road conditions are retained.

The CHP source is incomplete on April 3, 2026. That date is marked as incomplete in the HTML instead of being treated as a day with almost no incidents. Traffic speed and weather remain available on that date.

### 1.4 *NOAA GHCNh Weather*

The weather data come from seven NOAA airport stations in and around the study area: Los Angeles, Long Beach, Burbank, Santa Ana, Ontario, Riverside, and Palm Springs.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Station**</span>: NOAA station ID.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Station Name**</span>: NOAA station name.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Time**</span>: Observation time converted from UTC to Los Angeles local time.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Latitude**</span> and <span style="color: blue;">**Longitude**</span>: Weather-station coordinates.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Temperature**</span>: Air temperature in degrees Celsius.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Wind Speed**</span>: Wind speed in metres per second.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Visibility**</span>: Visibility in kilometres.

* <span style="color: blue;">**Precipitation**</span>: Reported precipitation in millimetres.

* **Precipitation Period**: Distinguishes 5-minute precipitation from other reported precipitation values.

* **Source URL**: NOAA source for the observation.

Each road link uses the nearest NOAA station. Temperature, wind, and visibility are placed on the 5-minute time index and carried forward for no more than 90 minutes. Previous-hour rainfall is calculated when the 5-minute reporting window is complete. A separate NOAA precipitation total is used when the 5-minute window is incomplete and that total is available.

NOAA observations describe conditions near the weather station. They are not measurements taken directly on each road link.

## 2. Data Cleaning

The traffic, incident, and weather records are cleaned before the HTML is built.

For traffic speed, `ML` stations with valid coordinates and postmiles are retained. Average speeds from 1 to 100 mph are kept, including records whose `Samples` or `Percentage Observed` value is zero. Those two fields are counted as quality indicators and are not used to remove speeds from the map. Invalid speed formats, out-of-range values, invalid timestamps, and records outside April 2026 are treated as missing. Columns not needed for the map, including lane-level repetitions, are left out of the cleaned traffic file. Stations are ordered by freeway, direction, and absolute postmile. Adjacent stations are connected when the coordinate gap and postmile gap are within the road-link limits.

CHP events outside D7, D8, and D12 are removed. The monthly archive is used when it is available; daily files are the fallback. Duplicate incident IDs are reduced to one record. Each remaining incident is matched to a road link, then its detail messages and speed comparison are added.

Weather observations are placed on the same 5-minute time index as the traffic data. Temperature, wind speed, and visibility can be carried forward for up to 90 minutes. Rainfall is calculated for the previous hour only when the reporting window is complete or NOAA gives a separate total.

## 3. HTML

The HTML covers all 8,640 five-minute intervals in April 2026. OpenStreetMap provides the basemap.

### 3.1 *Traffic Speed*

Road links are coloured by the current speed. The time slider changes the map in 5-minute steps, and the play control moves through the month automatically. Pause and reset controls are also included.

Clicking a road link gives its freeway, direction, endpoint station IDs, current speed, normal speed, speed deficit, active incident count, nearest NOAA station, and previous-hour rainfall. Station points and the road casing can be turned on or off.

Normal speed is the median for the same road link, weekday, and 5-minute time in April. Speed deficit is calculated as:

$$
\text{speed deficit} = \max(0,\ \text{normal speed} - \text{current speed})
$$

### 3.2 *CHP Incidents*

An active incident is marked by a red diamond and its matched road link receives a dashed outline. Incident markers appear only during the interval in which the event is active.

Incidents can be filtered by type. The incident panel lists the active events at the selected time. Selecting an event moves the map to its location and opens its description, CHP detail messages, report and end times, matched road, and previous-hour rainfall.

Events without a reliable road-link match remain visible at their CHP coordinates. Their popups do not report a speed effect.

The event popup compares the median speed on the matched road link during four periods:

* The 30 minutes before the event.

* The active event interval.

* The 30 minutes after the reported end time.

* The normal speed for the same weekday and 5-minute time on other dates.

At least two valid 5-minute observations are required for the before, during, and after values. The normal value excludes the event date and requires at least two other reference dates. The popup reports the change from the pre-event speed and the difference from normal speed. These comparisons describe the observed speed pattern on the matched link. They do not identify the incident as the cause of the change.

A warning appears on April 3 because the CHP source for that date is incomplete.

### 3.3 *Weather*

The weather panel gives the number of stations reporting rain, median temperature, median wind speed, lowest visibility, and highest previous-hour rainfall at the selected time.

Weather values in road and incident popups come from the NOAA station nearest to the matched road link.

### 3.4 *Congestion Ranking*

The ranking lists up to eight road links with the largest current speed deficits. Missing and zero speeds are excluded. A link enters the ranking when its deficit is at least 3 mph and its current speed is below 60 mph.

Each row gives the freeway and direction, endpoint station IDs, current speed, speed deficit, incident status, and rainfall. Selecting a row moves the map to that road link.

### 3.5 *Current-Time Summary*

The map also gives the selected time, average road-link speed, number of active incidents, highest previous-hour rainfall, number of road links with speed values, and number of weather stations reporting rain.
